lines.text: Why does hearing your own voice played back in a recording feel so completely cringe and unfamiliar?
When you listen to yourself speak, you are actually hearing two completely different sound paths.
You hear airborne sound waves entering your outer ears, just like everyone else does.
Simultaneously, your vocal cord vibrations travel upward through your own facial bones and skull.
Bone conduction deepens lower frequencies, making your voice sound richer and deeper in your own head.
An audio recording captures only the airborne sound waves, revealing how your voice actually sounds to the world.
Don't worry; everyone hates their recorded voice, but to others, it sounds completely normal.
